m.s: Trim any thick silverskin off {beef_cheek}, pat dry and season well. Heat a drizzle of oil in a heavy pot over high heat and brown the cheeks hard on all sides, about 8 minutes. Set aside.
Turn the heat down to medium. Cook finely diced {onion} and {carrot} for 10 minutes until soft. Add crushed {garlic} and {tompaste} and cook for 2 minutes until dark.

Add {tintom}, {rosemary}, {stockpowder} and enough water to just cover the cheeks, then return the beef. Cover and simmer on the lowest heat (or in a 150°C oven) for 3½ hours, until a spoon cuts straight through the meat.
Lift out the cheeks and shred them with two forks, discarding the rosemary stalks. Simmer the sauce uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes until thick and glossy, then stir in {butter} and the beef.
Cook {pasta} in a big pot of well-salted boiling water until al dente. Scoop out a mug of the water, then drain.
Toss the pasta through the sauce with a splash of the pasta water until it coats every piece. Finish with grated {parm} and chopped {parsley}.

l: Even better the next day. Loosen with a splash of water when reheating. Keeps 4 days in the fridge, and the sauce freezes well.
g: GF pasta in its own pot. Check the stock powder.
